description: MiTra: A Drone-Based Trajectory Data for an All-Traffic-State Inclusive Freeway with Ramps is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Ankit Anil Chaudhari et al. Traffic flow modeling is used in transportation engineering and urban planning, particularly in complex scenarios such as lane-changing and movements at ramps. However, obtaining high-quality trajectory data remains challenging, especially in urban environments where traditional methods like stationary cameras fall short. Existing drone-based datasets often lack full coverage of traffic states and critical merging and diverging behaviors at ramps. Coverage: not stated; published in 2025. Formats: CSV, Image. The data are held in Technische Universität Dresden and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is Attribution 4.0 International, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked, and the coverage and resolution are those of the abstract only. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
